chunks: The false testifier — his feet do not move until the Fire is made obligatory for him.

key_terms.الزُّور: Falsehood, deception, false testimony — used in classical jurisprudence specifically for perjury
key_terms.تَجِبَ: Becomes obligatory / is necessitated — indicating the certainty and immediacy of the punishment
key_terms.شَاهِدُ الزُّورِ: False testifier / witness of falsehood — one who gives perjured testimony in court

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for false testimony (shahid al-zur) according to Imam al-Sadiq in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) warns with striking immediacy that the punishment for false testimony is not deferred to a distant judgment: the Fire becomes certain for the false witness before he even steps away from the act. In early Islamic legal discourse, false testimony (shahid al-zur) was considered one of the gravest social sins because it could unjustly condemn the innocent and corrupt the entire judicial system. The phrasing 'his feet do not move' conveys that the consequence is instantaneous and inescapable — spiritual ruin is sealed the moment the lie is uttered in testimony.
